paren.optional_part.test: a balanced pair touching a letter outside it on either side, or whose content begins or ends with '-'
paren.optional_part.means: Optional letters or an optional word part, read with or without it: way(s), (day)light, (re)unite, (Beth-)Geder; one reading.

paren.uncertainty.means: The provider flags the rendering before it as uncertain; one reading.

paren.equivalence_aside.test: a balanced pair whose content begins with '='
paren.equivalence_aside.means: An aside giving what the reading amounts to: to catch up with (= happen); one reading.
examples: נשג: to catch up with (= happen)

paren.extension_aside.test: a balanced pair whose content begins with '>'
paren.extension_aside.means: An aside giving the extended sense of the word before it: heart (> allegiance); one reading.
examples: אחרנית: (God) turns someone's heart (> allegiance) back (to himself)

paren.grammatical_label.test: a balanced pair whose content ends with ':' or is 'pl'
paren.grammatical_label.means: A grammatical label on the reading (plural); one reading.

paren.list_inside.test: a balanced pair at a word boundary whose content holds a comma
paren.list_inside.means: The typical objects or settings of the reading, listed inside one qualifier: to wear (clothes, armor); one reading, and the commas inside are the qualifier's own.
examples: חרם: (someone with a) split, disfigured (ear, nose, or lip)

paren.argument_placeholder.test: a balanced pair at a word boundary whose content holds someone, something, somewhere, one, one's, oneself, another, X or Y
paren.argument_placeholder.means: The slot the context fills (the object, possessor or partner of the verb): to beat (one's) breast; one reading.
examples: שפת: to consign (someone) to the dust of death

paren.qualifier.test: any other balanced pair at a word boundary
paren.qualifier.means: An optional or explanatory word or phrase inside the reading (the object, a complement, the domain): to flow (with tears), (most) holy place; one reading.

paren.opener_never_closed.test: a '(' with no ')' after it in the route

paren.closer_with_nothing_open.test: a ')' with no '(' open before it in the route
paren.closer_with_nothing_open.means: A closer with nothing open: either the provider's own text carries it, or the ingest cut the provider's item inside its parenthesis; not a division.

apos.possessive_s.test: an apostrophe between a letter and 's' that ends the word
apos.possessive_s.means: Possessive inside a word (one's, someone's, God's); one reading.
examples: פלס: to give free course to (one's) anger

apos.plural_possessive.test: an apostrophe after a word-final 's', followed by a space or the end
apos.plural_possessive.means: Plural possessive inside a name (Wildgoats' Rocks); one reading.

gt.literal_to_extended.test: '>' at depth 0 whose left side is not a quoted phrase
gt.literal_to_extended.means: One reading: the literal or source sense on the left, the extended sense the word carries in this use on the right (dwelling > behavior).
examples: צלח: to advance > to become as (queen)
חנף: to be defiled > to be destroyed
סכך: to cover (one's) feet > to relieve oneself

gt.quoted_idiom_to_meaning.test: '>' at depth 0 whose left side is a phrase in double quotes
gt.quoted_idiom_to_meaning.means: One reading: an idiom quoted literally on the left, what it comes to on the right ("deep of tongue" > obscure speech).

gt.inside_parentheses.means: Inside an aside, the extended sense of the word before the parenthesis; one reading.
examples: אחרנית: (God) turns someone's heart (> allegiance) back (to himself)

hyphen.compound_word.test: '-' between two letters where neither joined word is capitalized
hyphen.compound_word.means: Joins a compound word (dwelling-place, father-in-law); one reading.
examples: קשח: to cause to be stiff-necked

hyphen.name_join.test: '-' between two letters where a joined word is capitalized
hyphen.name_join.means: Joins the parts of a place or personal name (Paddan-Aram, El-roi); one reading.

hyphen.optional_part.means: Part of an optional word piece written in parentheses (plough(-point), (Beth-)Geder); one reading.

comma.inside_parentheses.means: Lists the members of one qualifier (objects, settings); the reading is the whole route.
examples: חרם: (someone with a) split, disfigured (ear, nose, or lip)

comma.complete_infinitives.test: ',' at depth 0 where every comma piece of the route begins 'to '
comma.complete_infinitives.means: Packs two complete renderings of one meaning into one gloss: to go, to arrive.
examples: סור: to pass from, to be removed

comma.complete_nominal.test: ',' at depth 0, route not beginning 'to ', where no comma piece holds a parenthesis or the words of/to/and/or/whether and every piece is at most 3 words
comma.complete_nominal.means: Packs two or more complete renderings of one meaning into one gloss: loins, sides; Ephrathah, Ephrath.

comma.copula_elliptic.test: ',' at depth 0 where the first piece is exactly 'to be' and the next begins 'become'
comma.copula_elliptic.means: Packs 'to be X' and 'to become X' with X written once: to be, become weak. Two readings in meaning, but the first piece alone ('to be') is not one.

comma.verb_head_distributed.test: ',' at depth 0 where the first piece begins 'to ' and a later piece does not
comma.verb_head_distributed.means: Packs renderings of one verb with the infinitive (and any causative or passive frame) written once on the first: to cause (mountains) to skip, jump. Two readings in meaning, but a later piece alone ('jump') is not one.
examples: צלח: to possess, grip, take control
רקד: to cause (mountains) to skip, jump

comma.list_with_edge_parenthesis.test: ',' at depth 0, route not beginning 'to ', where the first piece begins with '(' or the last piece ends with ')'
comma.list_with_edge_parenthesis.means: Packs renderings under a qualifier written once at the edge of the list, whose scope over the other members the provider does not write: (images of) hemorrhoids, tumors, ulcers. Divides in meaning; a piece alone would lose or misplace the qualifier.
examples: חרם: (someone with a) split, disfigured (ear, nose, or lip)
שלשום: (what used to be done) before, in the past
כפרת: cover, lid (of the ark of the covenant)

comma.of_head_distributed.test: ',' at depth 0 where the first piece holds ' of ' and every later piece is one word
comma.of_head_distributed.means: Packs a head phrase written once with several completions: mouth of well, cave, pit. Divides in meaning; 'cave' alone is not a reading of the word.
examples: פה: mouth of well, cave, pit

comma.before_subordinate_clause.test: ',' at depth 0 followed by a piece beginning whether/which/who/when/where/if/although/because/that/while
comma.before_subordinate_clause.means: Sets off a clause that qualifies the reading: everyone, whether great or small; one reading.
examples: כפה: everyone, whether great or small

period.ellipsis.test: '.' inside a run of exactly three periods
period.ellipsis.means: An ellipsis: the slot the context fills (at the age of ...); one reading.
examples: פה: on this side ... on the other side
או: if ... (then God may punish me!)

q.parenthesized_uncertainty.means: The provider flags the rendering before it as uncertain; one reading.

q.between_uncertain_alternatives.test: '?' followed by a space and a letter
q.between_uncertain_alternatives.means: Closes one uncertain rendering before the next (plaque? tablet? panel? block?). Divides in meaning; not separated, since the mark belongs to the piece before it.

q.route_final_interrogative.test: route-final '?' where the route begins with an interrogative (where, how, why, what, when, who, really, truly, is, are, optionally after from/for/to)
q.route_final_interrogative.means: The reading is itself a question word or question (where?, is it true?); one reading.

q.route_final_uncertainty.test: route-final '?' where the route does not begin with an interrogative
q.route_final_uncertainty.means: The provider flags the rendering as uncertain (chisel?, to cheat?); one reading.

quote.literal_before_eq_or_gt.test: a double-quote pair whose closing quote is followed by ' =' or ' >'
quote.literal_before_eq_or_gt.means: Marks the literal wording of an idiom before its meaning; one reading.
examples: אם: "the mother of the way" = the parting of a way
אטר: "closed on the right hand" = left-handed

quote.whole_route_sound.test: a double-quote pair enclosing the whole route, with no '=' or '>'
quote.whole_route_sound.means: Marks the reading as a sound or cry given as written ("heidad"); one reading.

excl.route_final.means: The reading is an exclamation (behold!, alas!); one reading.

excl.between_exclamations.test: '!' at depth 0 followed by a space and a letter
excl.between_exclamations.means: Closes one exclamation before the next (woe! alas!). Divides in meaning; not separated, since the mark belongs to the piece before it.

excl.inside_parentheses.means: Ends an aside that completes the formula (if ... (then God may punish me!)); one reading.
examples: או: if ... (then God may punish me!)

eq.quoted_literal_to_meaning.test: '=' preceded by a closing double quote and a space
eq.quoted_literal_to_meaning.means: One reading: an idiom quoted literally, then what it means ("straight way" = safe journey).
examples: אם: "the mother of the way" = the parting of a way
אטר: "closed on the right hand" = left-handed

eq.inside_parentheses.means: Inside an aside, what the reading amounts to; one reading.
examples: נשג: to catch up with (= happen)

eq.route_initial.means: Opens a gloss that states what the word amounts to in a given use; one reading.

eq.rendering_to_explanation.test: '=' at depth 0 between two unquoted phrases
eq.rendering_to_explanation.means: One reading: a rendering, then the explanation of what it denotes (filthy things = objects stained by menstruation).
examples: דוה: filthy things = objects stained by menstruation

colon.label_in_parentheses.means: Ends a grammatical label ((plural:) cavalry); one reading.

colon.between_two_nouns.means: Stands between a masculine and a feminine noun (sorcerer: sorceress). Divides in meaning; not separated (one route).

slash.spaced_alternatives.test: '/' with a space on each side
slash.spaced_alternatives.means: Alternatives completing one head phrase written once (juice of purslane / mallows). Divides in meaning; 'mallows' alone is not the reading.

slash.unspaced_alternation.means: Alternation inside one reading (his/her); one reading.
examples: אשם: to make someone bear his/her guilt

backslash.stray_before_word.test: '\' after a space and before a letter
backslash.stray_before_word.means: A stray character in the provider's text (to cause to bring \birth; the same record also has 'to cause to bring forth'); one reading.

bracket.editorial_note.test: a square-bracket pair enclosing the whole route
bracket.editorial_note.means: An editorial note, not a rendering: the provider says the word is left untranslated in some use.
